findings.evidence: grep -rn 'RatSlash|Cusps/Rat' returns only HeckeSlash/Cusps.lean:40; `ls Cusps/Rat/` shows `Basic.lean  Slash.lean`.
findings.issue: Module doc says the general statement "lives in `ModularForms/Cusps/RatSlash.lean`"; no such module exists — the file added by this PR is `ModularForms/Cusps/Rat/Slash.lean` (module `TauCeti.NumberTheory.ModularForms.Cusps.Rat.Slash`, imported on line 9).

findings.evidence: Cusps/Rat/Slash.lean:54-56 and 62-64: the per-summand step is exactly the atomic statement, discharged inside a `fun i _ ↦` with nothing from the sum.
findings.fix: State `OnePoint.isZeroAt_rat_slash (g : GL (Fin 2) ℚ) (hf …) (hc …) : c.IsZeroAt (f ∣[k] g) k` and the `isBoundedAt_` twin, then derive the sum versions as `IsZeroAt.sum fun i _ ↦ isZeroAt_rat_slash k (g i) hf hc`.
findings.issue: Only the `Finset`-sum form is exposed, but the reusable atom is the single rational slash: the body of each lemma is `rw [ModularForm.rat_slash]; exact IsZeroAt.smul_iff.mp (hf _ (hc.smul_map_ratCast _))` applied per summand. A consumer holding one rational slash — e.g. the extra `p ∤ N` term added to `heckeSlashUpperTri`, or any `f ∣[k] g` — cannot use the sum lemma without `Finset.sum_singleton` contortions and will re-open-code the very lines this PR exists to delete.

summary: The new surface is minimal, hides no bodies, and leaves no compatibility artifact, but the module doc points at a nonexistent path and the factored-out API omits the single-slash atom the proof actually consumes.
